MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Simplify 5x + 3y − 2x + y. (1 mark)
   A. 3x + 4y
   B. 7x + 4y
   C. 7xy
   D. 3x + 2y

2. Simplify 7x − 4x. (1 mark)
   A. 28x
   B. 3
   C. 11x
   D. 3x

3. Simplify 3a + 2a. (1 mark)
   A. 5aa
   B. 5
   C. 5a
   D. 6a

4. A rope 9 m 60 cm long is cut into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 2 m 40 cm
   B. 9 m 56 cm
   C. 2 m 50 cm
   D. 4 m 80 cm

5. Change 908 cm to metres and centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 9 m 8 cm
   B. 90 cm
   C. 9 m 58 cm
   D. 10 m 8 cm

6. A rope 5 m 25 cm long is cut into 3 equal pieces. How long is each piece? (1 mark)
   A. 3 m 50 cm
   B. 1 m 75 cm
   C. 5 m 22 cm
   D. 1 m 85 cm

7. Rectangle P has 3 rows and 10 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 5 columns. Which has the bigger area? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle P
   B. It cannot be told
   C. Rectangle Q
   D. They are equal

8. What does area measure? (1 mark)
   A. How much water a container holds
   B. How long a line is
   C. How much flat surface a shape covers
   D. How heavy an object is

9. How can you compare the areas of two sheets of paper without measuring? (1 mark)
   A. Count the number of corners
   B. Put one on top of the other and see which one sticks out
   C. Measure their masses
   D. Fold both into halves and count folds only

10. Which statement about a cube is true? (1 mark)
   A. Its length is double its width
   B. It has only 4 faces
   C. Its length, width and height are equal
   D. It has no corners

11. How many blocks are needed to build a cube 5 blocks long, 5 blocks wide and 5 blocks high? (1 mark)
   A. 25
   B. 125
   C. 15
   D. 55

12. One layer of a cuboid has 24 blocks and there are 5 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 29 blocks
   B. 115 blocks
   C. 120 blocks
   D. 144 blocks

13. What is 7 1/2 L − 3 3/4 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 1/2 L
   B. 3 3/4 L
   C. 4 L
   D. 4 1/4 L

14. How many 1/2 L bottles can be filled from 12 L of juice? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 24
   C. 6
   D. 18

15. Which is the best instrument for comparing the mass of a mango with known masses? (1 mark)
   A. A ruler
   B. A clock
   C. A beam balance
   D. A measuring jug

16. What is 1 3/4 kg + 2 1/4 kg? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 kg
   B. 4 kg
   C. 4 1/4 kg
   D. 4 1/2 kg

17. Which unit do we use to measure the mass of a bag of maize flour? (1 mark)
   A. Metre
   B. Kilogram
   C. Centimetre
   D. Litre

18. In which direction do shadows point in the early morning? (1 mark)
   A. Towards the west
   B. They do not point anywhere
   C. Towards the east
   D. Straight up

19. How many days are in 6 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 30 days
   B. 42 days
   C. 144 days
   D. 49 days

20. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 2 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 3. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 3:15
   B. 2:15
   C. 2:45
   D. 2:03

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. A learner says 3 weeks is 20 days. Explain her mistake and give the correct number of days. (3 marks)

22. A classroom floor is covered with 15 rows of 10 tiles. How many tiles are used? If 6 tiles are broken and must be replaced, how many tiles are unbroken? (4 marks)

23. Explain why we should change lengths to centimetres before adding 3 m 45 cm and 2 m 80 cm. (3 marks)

24. Find the volume of a cuboid that is 6 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 3 blocks high. Show your working. (3 marks)

25. The floor of a shop has 8 rows of 12 square tiles. How many tiles are on the floor? (3 marks)

26. Subtract 2 hours 35 minutes from 5 hours 20 minutes. (3 marks)

27. An L-shaped garden has sides of 6 m, 2 m, 3 m, 2 m, 3 m and 4 m. Find its perimeter. (3 marks)

28. A matatu carries m passengers. At a stop 8 get in and 3 get out. Write and simplify an expression for the number of passengers now. (3 marks)

29. Give two differences between perimeter and area. (3 marks)

30. A cuboid has a volume of 60 blocks. One layer has 12 blocks. How many layers does it have? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #5 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 3x + 4y
   Only like terms can be joined. 5x + 3y − 2x + y = 3x + 4y.

2. D — 3x
   Only like terms can be joined. 7x − 4x = 3x.

3. C — 5a
   Only like terms can be joined. 3a + 2a = 5a.

4. A — 2 m 40 cm
   960 ÷ 4 = 240 cm = 2 m 40 cm.

5. A — 9 m 8 cm
   908 ÷ 100 = 9 remainder 8. So 908 cm = 9 m 8 cm.

6. B — 1 m 75 cm
   525 ÷ 3 = 175 cm = 1 m 75 cm.

7. D — They are equal
   P = 3 × 10 = 30 and Q = 6 × 5 = 30. They are equal.

8. C — How much flat surface a shape covers
   Area is the amount of flat surface covered by a shape.

9. B — Put one on top of the other and see which one sticks out
   Placing one surface on the other shows which is bigger.

10. C — Its length, width and height are equal
   A cube has 6 equal square faces, so its length, width and height are the same.

11. B — 125
   5 × 5 = 25 per layer and 25 × 5 = 125 blocks.

12. C — 120 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 24 × 5 = 120 blocks.

13. B — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 7 1/2 L − 3 3/4 L = 3 3/4 L.

14. B — 24
   Each litre fills 2 half-litre bottles, so 12 L fills 12 × 2 = 24 bottles.

15. C — A beam balance
   A beam balance compares an object with known masses.

16. B — 4 kg
   Work with the whole kilograms first and then the parts. 1 3/4 kg + 2 1/4 kg = 4 kg.

17. B — Kilogram
   Mass is measured in kilograms.

18. A — Towards the west
   The Sun rises in the east, so morning shadows point west.

19. B — 42 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 6 × 7 = 42 days.

20. B — 2:15
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 3 shows 3 × 5 = 15 minutes, so the time is 2:15.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 week has 7 days, so 3 weeks is 3 × 7 = 21 days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 days in a week, 1 mark for multiplying by 3, 1 mark for 21 days.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: 150 tiles; 144 tiles unbroken
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 15 × 10, 1 mark for 150, 1 mark for 150 − 6, 1 mark for 144.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: When both lengths are in centimetres we can add them like ordinary numbers: 345 + 280 = 625 cm. This avoids mistakes with regrouping 100 cm into 1 m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for using one unit, 1 mark for adding, 1 mark for reference to regrouping.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 72 blocks
   Working / marking points: 6 × 4 = 24 blocks in a layer (1 mark); 24 × 3 (1 mark); 72 blocks (1 mark).

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: 96 tiles
   Working / marking points: 8 × 12 (1 mark); 80 + 16 (1 mark); 96 tiles (1 mark).

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: Change 5 h 20 min to 4 h 80 min (1 mark); 80 − 35 = 45 min (1 mark); 4 − 2 = 2 h, so 2 h 45 min (1 mark).

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 20 m
   Working / marking points: 6 + 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 20 m. 2 marks for adding all six sides, 1 mark for the unit.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: m + 8 − 3 = m + 5
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for m + 8, 1 mark for taking away 3, 1 mark for simplifying to m + 5.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Perimeter is the distance round the edge and is measured in units of length such as cm. Area is the flat surface inside the shape and is measured in square units.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the meaning of each and 1 mark for the units.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5 layers
   Working / marking points: 60 ÷ 12 = 5. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the answer.
